novelty_note: Williams %R overbought/oversold entry with long-EMA trend filter; standard reversal-in-trend idea, low novelty

title: EMA-crossover with lookback + pullback confirmation grid EA (Advance Robot #14)
entry_long: EMA_fast crossed above EMA_slow at any candle within lookback window candle_id15-24, EMA_fast still above EMA_slow currently, and current price pulls back below EMA_fast -> buy 0.1 lot
entry_short: mirror: EMA_fast crossed below EMA_slow within candle_id15-24 window, still below currently, and price pulls back above EMA_fast -> sell 0.1 lot
exit: close all when combined profit>10 pips; trailing stop 10/step1 after trade count>=2 (follow-mode); follow-mode grid every 15 pip; reverse-mode adds on opposite-direction engulfing signal with L_Plus=0.05 increment
escalation_cap: none
buildon_idea: add max-order/lot cap; author's 5yr in-sample result had relative DD ~58% - needs flat-lot and OOS check before any deploy consideration
novelty_note: scans a 10-candle window for a prior EMA cross plus a pullback-to-fast-EMA confirmation before entry, reducing false immediate-cross entries; moderate novelty vs plain crossover EAs

title: EMA-cross martingale gold scalper (Go Robot scouting basic)
entry_long: EMA_fast(5) crosses above EMA_slow(12) -> buy 0.1 lot, SL=100 pip, TP=100 pip
entry_short: EMA_fast(5) crosses below EMA_slow(12) -> sell 0.1 lot, SL=100 pip, TP=100 pip
exit: fixed SL/TP=100 pip per order; on TP-hit (win) next order in same direction reopens at base lot 0.1; on SL-hit (loss) next order reverses direction and doubles lot size (lot_x=2, uncapped repetition)
escalation_cap: none
buildon_idea: add a max-step cap (e.g. 5-6 doublings) or switch escalation to linear-add/log to remove ruin risk; flat-lot test (disable doubling) to check if the EMA5/12 cross alone has any edge before crediting the martingale for the demoed profit; author explicitly states this EA is not usable in all market conditions
novelty_note: plain EMA cross entry with classic double-on-loss / reset-on-win martingale money management; low novelty, high structural risk as shown (no cap)

title: Three-candle continuation pattern (soldiers/crows) grid EA (Advance Robot #15)
entry_long: candle_id4, candle_id3, candle_id2 all bullish (min body 4 pip) and candle_id1 close still above candle_id2 open (shallow pullback, not breaking down) -> buy 0.1 lot fixed
entry_short: mirror: candle_id4/3/2 all bearish and candle_id1 close still below candle_id2 open (shallow pullback) -> sell 0.1 lot fixed
exit: close all when combined profit>10 pips; trailing stop 10/step1 after trade count>=2 (follow-mode); follow-mode grid every 15 pip; reverse-mode adds on opposite-direction engulfing signal with L_Plus (0.01 used in test) lot increment
escalation_cap: none
buildon_idea: author himself suggests: add a max-order cap (e.g. MaxOrder=15) to limit grid risk, and swap the engulfing reversal filter for RSI/Stochastic/Williams%R/EMA-cross as alternate confirmation - both directly actionable; 5yr in-sample gain only 62% (weaker than sibling EAs), worth comparing after fixes
novelty_note: three-bar continuation (soldiers/crows) with a shallow-pullback filter as first-entry trigger; author flags it as an unoptimized teaching example

title: Auto-drawn trendline break + EMA50 confirm grid EA (Advance Robot #16)
indicators: auto-drawn trendline (highest/lowest over N candles, N=50 or 90 vs 15)

novelty_note: auto-generates a trendline object from rolling highest/lowest-over-N reference points (not a fixed indicator) as a breakout signal, then confirms with EMA cross; the auto-trendline construction itself is a reusable building block worth cataloging

title: Bollinger Band 2-candle reversal grid EA (Advance Trading Robot 17)

title: Stochastic overbought/oversold 3-candle-momentum grid EA on XAUUSD M1 (rev.2, dynamic close-money)
entry_long: 3 consecutive bullish candles (ID1<ID2<ID3 shrinking wait: body ID1>ID2>ID3 largest first) + Stochastic < 30 (oversold, adjusted from default 20)
entry_short: 3 consecutive bearish candles with decreasing body size + Stochastic > 70 (overbought, adjusted from default 80)

title: 3-candle momentum expanding-body pattern grid EA with backtest-mode comparison (Control Points vs Every Tick)
entry_long: 3 consecutive bullish candles with increasing body size (ID1>ID2>ID3, largest most recent) -> buy
entry_short: 3 consecutive bearish candles with increasing body size (ID1>ID2>ID3) -> sell

entry_short: Daily RSI(14)<40 (downtrend) AND M15 RSI(14) crosses below 70 -> sell 0.01 lot
exit: no SL/TP initial; Follow-Train mode pyramids fixed 0.01 lot every 20pip grid when in profit + trailing stop 10pip after 2 trades; Reverse-Train mode (martingale recovery) adds lot_BS+=L_Plus(0.01) each step on opposite-side loss, confirmed by engulfing reversal at 20pip grid, closes both legs when combined profit>10pip
escalation_cap: none stated (no order-count cap on Reverse-Train escalation)
buildon_idea: add explicit max-step cap to Reverse-Train lot escalation (e.g. Max_Order like EX102's 20); flat-lot test the Reverse-Train branch to confirm the RSI+engulfing recovery entry has edge independent of martingale sizing
novelty_note: MTF RSI trend/entry combined with dual-mode follow/reverse martingale-grid switching logic; moderate novelty in the mode-switch mechanism

title: Gold scalping dual RSI (Daily trend + M5 entry) with grid pyramid and 3-candle SL
entry_long: Daily RSI(14)>60 AND M5 RSI(14) crosses above 30 -> buy 0.01 lot, SL = lowest low of candle ID1-3
entry_short: Daily RSI(14)<40 AND M5 RSI(14) crosses below 70 -> sell 0.01 lot, SL = highest high of candle ID1-3
exit: initial SL from 3-candle lookback, no TP; grid-add fixed 0.01 lot every 25pip in trend direction; telling_Money_loss trailing stop caps loss at $10 after 2 trades open (step $1)
escalation_cap: loss capped via telling_Money_loss $10 (not order-count capped)
buildon_idea: has SL + money-loss cap already; extend to other symbol/TF pairs and verify the grid-add pyramid doesn't multiply risk beyond the $10 cap under fast-move slippage
novelty_note: same core dual-RSI idea as EX104 but simplified to flat-lot grid with hard SL; low-medium novelty

title: Candlestick reversal (5pip threshold) with Follow/Reverse-train recovery
entry_long: candle ID1 bearish (min body>=5pip) AND current price > candle ID1 close by >5pip -> buy 0.01 lot
entry_short: candle ID1 bullish (min body>=5pip) AND current price < candle ID1 close by >5pip -> sell 0.01 lot
exit: no SL/TP; Follow-Train pyramids fixed 0.01 lot every 20pip grid + trailing stop 10pip after 2 trades; Reverse-Train martingale-recovery adds lot_BS+=L_Plus(0.01) each step at 20pip grid confirmed by opposite engulfing, closes at combined profit>10pip
escalation_cap: none stated
buildon_idea: add a step cap to the Reverse-Train martingale (same design gap as EX104); backtest result was weak (13.85% over 5yr) so build-on should focus on filtering the reversal entry before scaling risk further
novelty_note: reuses the EX104 follow/reverse-train framework on a plain candlestick-reversal signal instead of RSI; low novelty, weak backtest

title: Gold scalping candlestick reversal with explicitly unlimited grid pyramid
entry_long: candle ID1 bearish (min body>=50pip) AND current price > candle ID1 close by >50pip -> buy 0.01 lot, SL=lowest of 3-candle lookback
entry_short: candle ID1 bullish (min body>=50pip) AND current price < candle ID1 close by >50pip -> sell 0.01 lot, SL=highest of 3-candle lookback
exit: initial SL from 3-candle lookback, no TP; grid-add fixed 0.01 lot every 25pip, narrator explicitly states adds are unlimited ('ไม่จำกัด'); trailing stop 100pip (step for gold) after 2 trades
escalation_cap: none — narrator states pyramiding is unlimited
buildon_idea: add explicit max-order cap to the unlimited pyramid (fixed-lot so risk is linear not exponential, but still needs a ceiling); has initial SL which is a plus — flat single-entry test to isolate the reversal entry edge before scaling grid count
novelty_note: evolution of EX106 into pure fixed-lot scalping grid without martingale sizing; the explicitly unlimited add count is the key risk difference

title: Gold zigzag breakout scalping with grid pyramid
entry_long: current price >= previous ZigZag High (ID1) -> breakout up -> buy 0.01 lot, SL=lowest of 3-candle lookback
entry_short: current price <= previous ZigZag Low (ID1) -> breakout down -> sell 0.01 lot, SL=highest of 3-candle lookback
exit: initial SL from 3-candle lookback, no TP; grid-add fixed 0.01 lot every 50pip in trend direction; telling_Stop trailing 100pip/step10 after 2 trades
escalation_cap: none stated — no max-order limit mentioned
buildon_idea: add explicit order cap to the grid pyramid; author recommends a low-spread account (2pip) — test on higher-spread brokers before deploy; also test flat single-entry (no pyramid) to isolate the zigzag-breakout edge
novelty_note: zigzag swing-break entry combined with fixed lot-pumping grid; the auto chart-object drawing (arrows/labels) is a reusable dev pattern more than a trading novelty

title: Gold scalping custom-math (arctan momentum angle) entry with grid and stuck-order cutloss
entry_long: Angle = (close[1]-close[2])/period > 0 -> buy 0.01 lot
entry_short: Angle < 0 -> sell 0.01 lot
exit: no direct SL; grid-add fixed 0.01 lot every 50pip in trend direction; telling_Money_loss trailing stop caps loss at $10 after 1 trade; additional Cut_loss_Money=-$10 force-closes any stuck/unrealized-loss position beyond -$10
escalation_cap: loss capped via telling_Money_loss $10 + Cut_loss_Money -$10 failsafe; no order-count cap
buildon_idea: already has dual money-based safety nets (trailing stop + stuck-order cutloss) — good build-on base; add a hard price SL as a third layer, and test the author's hinted complex/quaternion-math extension for entry quality
novelty_note: simple 2-candle slope/arctan momentum entry is low novelty as a signal, but the custom-math-in-nocode-tool technique is reusable; the stuck-order cutloss failsafe is worth cataloging separately

title: Gold scalping auto-trendline + EMA break confirmation with grid pyramid
entry_long: price above auto TR_LINE_buy (support trendline) AND price crosses above EMA(50) -> buy 0.01 lot
entry_short: price below auto TR_LINE_sell (resistance trendline) AND price crosses below EMA(50) -> sell 0.01 lot
exit: no SL/TP; grid-add fixed 0.01 lot every 50pip in trend direction; telling_Money_loss trailing stop caps loss at $10 after 1 trade
escalation_cap: loss capped via telling_Money_loss $10; no order-count cap
buildon_idea: add a hard SL layer; the auto-trendline-drawing technique (2-point regression from swing highs/lows) is reusable for other EAs; test dual-confirmation (trendline+EMA) vs EMA alone to check whipsaw reduction
novelty_note: dual-confirmation (auto trendline break + EMA cross) claimed as a 'safer' pyramiding trigger; the auto-trendline object-generation technique is the more reusable piece

title: Gold scalping ROC momentum + EMA cross with grid pyramid
entry_long: EMA(8) crosses above EMA(18) AND ROC(12)>0 -> buy 0.01 lot
entry_short: EMA(8) crosses below EMA(18) AND ROC(12)<0 -> sell 0.01 lot
exit: no SL/TP; grid-add fixed 0.01 lot every 35pip in trend direction; telling_Money_loss trailing stop caps loss at $10 after 1 trade
escalation_cap: loss capped via telling_Money_loss $10; no order-count cap
family: ROC momentum + EMA cross grid scalping
buildon_idea: add a hard SL layer; the custom-ROC-via-formula technique is reusable when a platform lacks a built-in ROC block; narrator claims the base EMA+ROC signal alone (with real SL/TP, no grid) can run for years without blowing up — worth verifying that claim separately from the grid-pyramid overlay
novelty_note: standard EMA-cross+momentum filter; the separate claim that the raw signal survives years unmodified is the more testable lead

title: Gold scalping support/resistance liquidity-sweep pullback + MACD(4,9,4) confirmation with grid pyramid
entry_long: price breaks below auto support (liquidity sweep) within 10 candles, pulls back above the support line, AND MACD(4,9,4)>0 -> buy 0.01 lot
entry_short: price breaks above auto resistance (liquidity sweep) within 10 candles, pulls back below the resistance line, AND MACD(4,9,4)<0 -> sell 0.01 lot
exit: no SL/TP; grid-add fixed 0.01 lot every 35pip in trend direction; telling_Money_loss trailing stop caps loss at $10 after 1 trade
escalation_cap: loss capped via telling_Money_loss $10; no order-count cap; unconfirmed breakout signal auto-expires/resets after 10 candles
family: S/R liquidity-sweep pullback + MACD grid scalping
buildon_idea: add a hard SL layer; the liquidity-sweep + pullback + MACD-confirmation entry logic (auto S/R lines, 10-candle signal expiry) is the most sophisticated/reusable entry filter in this batch — worth extracting into EDGE_CATALOG even if the grid-lot overlay itself isn't deployed as-is
novelty_note: liquidity-sweep + pullback + momentum-confirmation entry is meaningfully more sophisticated than the plain breakout/candlestick signals elsewhere in this batch — higher novelty

title: Gold Robot Scalping [RSI Divergence + ZigZag Swing]
entry_long: swing low detected (zigzag), price makes lower-low vs prior zigzag low while RSI makes higher-low at those points = bullish RSI divergence; buy_mode/sell_mode toggle gates direction (market-structure filter left unbuilt, defaulted True/True)
entry_short: mirror: swing high detected, price makes higher-high while RSI makes lower-high = bearish RSI divergence
exit: SL = custom price level from lowest/highest of prior 3 candles; TP = 200% of SL distance
escalation_cap: 2.0 lots (Volume Upper Limit)
buildon_idea: already capped at 2 lots; flat-lot test first (disable x2 multiply) to check entry-only edge; author notes it needs a real market-structure/trend filter (buy-only in uptrend, sell-only in downtrend) to be sustainable — build that filter before deploying
novelty_note: RSI-divergence via zigzag swing points is a common but reasonably rigorous mechanical implementation; draws trend/divergence lines on chart for visual confirm

title: Gold Robot Scalping [Fibonacci Retracement Grid, EMA-triggered]
entry_long: EMA5>EMA100 with distance<1000pips, triggered when EMA5 crosses down EMA12 -> draw fibo retracement over last 90 candles (low=ref1); price crossing up each of 5 fibo levels (0,50,61.8,78.6,100%) opens a buy in a separate magic-number group per level (0.01 lot each, no SL/TP)
entry_short: mirror: EMA5<EMA100, EMA5 crosses up EMA12 -> draw fibo Sell (high as ref1); price crossing down each of 5 fibo levels opens sell per group
exit: trailing stop 200/step5 pips applied across all 5 groups simultaneously; fibo lines deleted/redrawn on EMA cross reversal
escalation_cap: n/a (fixed 0.01 lot per level, no volume cap stated, but capped to 5 discrete group entries per side per fibo redraw)
buildon_idea: unoptimized per author; add position cap per group, test with SL/TP or trailing-only risk cage; explore swapping fixed 0.01 per level to linear/log scaling by level depth
novelty_note: auto-drawn Fibonacci retracement gated by dual-EMA trend + distance filter, with 5 separately-tracked magic-number entry groups per level — moderately novel structuring

title: Gold Robot Scalping [Triple-EMA Break Pattern + Grid]
entry_long: EMA3>EMA50 (distance<1500pips) and current candle closes crossing above BOTH EMA3 and EMA8 in the same bar (pullback-then-break pattern)
entry_short: mirror: EMA3<EMA50, candle crosses below both EMA3 and EMA8 same bar
exit: trailing stop 100/step5 pips, group-of-trade mode
escalation_cap: unspecified (no volume upper limit block shown)
buildon_idea: add explicit volume cap on grid add (currently unlimited every 50 pips against position); backtest showed 1920 orders/month at 6.17% relDD which suggests over-trading risk if cap missing — add position-count or lot cap before build-on
novelty_note: triple-EMA 'break both fast EMAs in one candle' pullback-continuation entry is a distinctive simple heuristic; common as general EMA-pullback family though

title: Gold Robot Scalping [Hedge Rebalance Martingale, original]
entry_long: open buy and sell simultaneously at start (Counter Pass One, once), then re-open in same direction whenever that side's position closes (TP or SL)
entry_short: mirror, simultaneous with buy leg
exit: SL=500pips, TP=500pips fixed per leg; on win, reset lot and reopen at start lot; on loss, lot doubles (capped) and reopens at the SL price
escalation_cap: 2.0 lots (Volume Upper Limit)
buildon_idea: already capped 2 lots with SL; flat-lot test first to isolate entry edge from martingale contribution; try linear-add lot law instead of x2 doubling to reduce tail risk
novelty_note: simultaneous buy+sell 'always in market' hedge rebalance with independent per-side martingale — later revised by author after user complaints about orders not firing and asymmetric buy/sell spacing (see EX116 revision)

title: Gold Robot Scalping [Hedge Rebalance Martingale, revision 1 + cut-loss]
entry_long: open buy+sell simultaneously once per minute if missing (changed from Counter Pass One to Once-per-minute check to fix users' orders-not-firing reports)
entry_short: mirror, checked once per minute
exit: no SL; TP=500pips only; when either side hits TP, immediately close the OPPOSITE side too (Trade Close action) instead of waiting for its own SL — keeps both legs synced/closing together; separate hard cut-loss: if consecutive losses on either side >=10, close both sides, send LINE notify alert, and terminate EA
escalation_cap: 2.0 lots (Volume Upper Limit), plus consecutive-loss(10) circuit breaker that force-closes and halts the EA
buildon_idea: good example of build-on: added consecutive-loss cut-loss + alerting on top of prior martingale version; still no per-trade SL (relies on TP-linked opposite-close) — consider adding a hard SL per leg in addition to the consecutive-loss breaker; user-reported live/demo order-firing issues fixed by switching timer block, worth reusing that fix pattern elsewhere
novelty_note: notable for its explicit iterative fix-based-on-user-feedback narrative: switched trigger block, added synced opposite-side close, added consecutive-loss cutoff + LINE notification — a good template for hardening a live-fielded martingale EA

title: Sideway Range Breakout + Engulfing (S/R lines, grid recovery)
entry_long: price below support line but within 100 pips of it, and a bullish engulfing pattern forms (body>=5pips, ID1 close > ID2 open)
entry_short: mirror: price above resistance line within 100 pips, bearish engulfing forms
exit: single-trade TP=30pips; if grid-recovery trades open (>1), TP=8pips pip-as-position across all; grid add every 20pips with lot increasing by +0.05 per add (L_BS + L_Plus); S/R lines auto-delete/redraw if price exceeds range by >100pips
escalation_cap: none stated numerically (lot grows by fixed +0.05 increment per grid step, no explicit cap block)
buildon_idea: add explicit lot/position cap on the 20-pip grid recovery ladder; author already suggests reducing sideway-range lot size (0.5->0.25) to cut max DD (51.2%->lower); tested 5.5yr EURUSD H1 with real gain — good build-on candidate, add hard cap + optionally pending-limit entries at S/R to avoid market-order spread cost
novelty_note: auto-detected dynamic sideway channel (drawn/deleted live) combined with engulfing confirmation at channel edges + asymmetric TP by trade count — reasonably distinctive mechanism; 5.7yr backtest is unusually long for this corpus

title: 4-Candlestick Reversal Pattern + Grid Recovery
entry_long: ID4,ID3 bearish; ID2,ID1 bullish; at least one bar in each pair has body>=7pips; close of ID1 > open of ID4
entry_short: mirror: ID4,ID3 bullish; ID2,ID1 bearish; close of ID1 < open of ID4
exit: single-trade TP=30pips; multi-trade (grid) TP=8pips pip-as-position; grid add every 20pips, lot +0.01 per add (linear)
escalation_cap: unspecified (no explicit volume cap block; lot grows by fixed +0.01 increments only)
buildon_idea: add explicit lot cap on the linear grid-add ladder; author reports 5.5yr EURUSD H1 backtest with >300% gain and only ~30% max DD — reasonable build-on candidate given linear (not multiplicative) lot law is already the safer variant; test cap + pending-limit entries
novelty_note: specific 4-candle down-down/up-up reversal-with-close-above-open4 filter is a fairly precise mechanical pattern definition; simple but not generic

title: Breakout of Big-Body Candle + Trend-Quality Filter (Snowball Grid)
indicators: FX DMA New Top/Bottom trend-quality indicator
entry_long: prior bearish candle with body>=100pips draws a 'LINE buy' at its high; price crossing above that line AND New Top confirms quality uptrend (10 lookback candles, min 200pips range, quality=8) triggers buy
entry_short: mirror: prior bullish candle body>=100pips draws 'LINE sell' at its low; price crossing below + New Bottom confirms downtrend
exit: trailing money-loss stop capped at $10 loss max per side (steps by $1); snowball add every 50pips in profit direction, unlimited adds until reversal hits the $10 cap
escalation_cap: $10 max loss (trailing money-loss cap), no explicit lot-count cap on the snowball adds
buildon_idea: author explicitly flags own parameters as under-tuned (min body 100pips too small for gold M15, suggests 500-1000+; min trend range 200pips too small, suggests 500+) — good candidate to re-test with author's own suggested wider filters before judging; trailing-money-loss cap is already a reasonable risk cage, worth reusing as a pattern elsewhere
novelty_note: uses FX DMA's built-in trend-quality scoring block (New Top/Bottom-in) as a mechanical trend filter layered on breakout-of-big-candle entry — moderately novel due to trend-quality gate; snowball (pyramid) add direction is toward profit not loss, distinguishing from martingale

title: MACD Divergence + Candle Pattern + Volume Confirmation (Martingale, TP=3x/5x SL)
entry_long: MACD bullish divergence AND candle ID2 bearish, ID1 bullish AND tick-volume(ID1) > tick-volume(ID2)
entry_short: mirror: MACD bearish divergence, ID2 bullish/ID1 bearish, volume(ID1)>volume(ID2)
exit: SL=custom price level (low/high of ID1); TP=percent-of-SL, tested at both 300% (1:3) and 500% (1:5) ratios
escalation_cap: unspecified (no explicit Volume Upper Limit block shown; multiply-on-loss=2x, reset to initial 0.01 on win)
buildon_idea: has SL and win-reset already; add an explicit lot/volume cap to remove the uncapped_martingale flag before deploying; idea (Sniper-Shot low-frequency, high win-rate divergence+volume confirmation) came from a live trader's manual strategy and tested well (5yr, >3800% at 1:5, low trade count 305) — worth building on with a hard cap added
novelty_note: triple-confirmation entry (MACD divergence + candle direction pattern + volume comparison) sourced from a manual trader's shared strategy, framed by author as a low-frequency 'Sniper Shot' style specifically to survive high-volatility regimes vs high-frequency scalping EAs

title: MACD Divergence + Candle Pattern + Volume Confirmation (Martingale, H4, live-vol context)
entry_long: same as sibling video: MACD bullish divergence + ID2 bearish/ID1 bullish + volume(ID1)>volume(ID2), explicitly framed for larger TFs (H1/H4+) to keep win-rate high with few trades
entry_short: mirror of long side
exit: SL=custom price level (low/high of ID1); TP=percent-of-SL (500% shown, i.e. 1:5)
escalation_cap: unspecified (multiply-on-loss=2x betting-martingale, reset to initial lot on win; no explicit volume cap block shown)
buildon_idea: presented explicitly by author as a response to a high-volatility market event (50000-point gold swings) as a lower-frequency 'Sniper Shot' alternative to always-scalping grid EAs; add explicit lot cap; duplicate of EX120(-CFQcF2EYNk) mechanism recorded on a different day/context with H4 framing — treat as same family/candidate, not a second distinct idea
novelty_note: same mechanism as sibling EX120 video; notable mainly for author's framing that Sniper-Shot low-frequency EAs survive volatility spikes better than always-in-market grid/scalp EAs — a portfolio-construction insight more than a new mechanism

title: T-Candlestick Pattern (3-bar) + Dual-EMA Trend Filter + Grid
entry_long: EMA8>EMA18 (uptrend filter) AND candle ID1 and ID3 both bullish with body>=100pips (ID2 direction ignored) AND close(ID1) > close(ID3)
entry_short: mirror: EMA8<EMA18, ID1 & ID3 bearish body>=100pips, close(ID1) < close(ID3)
exit: no fixed SL/TP; grid add every 50pips in profit direction (snowball), managed via trailing stop group-of-trade at 100pips/step5pips
escalation_cap: n/a (fixed 0.01 lot per add, no cap block, but adds are snowball/profit-direction not martingale)
buildon_idea: add explicit SL per entry group in addition to trailing-stop-group risk control; combine EMA trend filter (already present) with tighter body-size threshold tuned per instrument/TF as author notes 100pips is instrument/TF-dependent; test flat-lot (already flat here) across more symbol/TF pairs since lot law is fixed not escalating — lower risk build-on candidate
novelty_note: 3-bar directional-body pattern (ignoring middle bar) plus simple dual-EMA trend gate and snowball grid; moderate novelty from the ID2-agnostic 3-bar pattern definition

title: 3-candle doji reversal (engulf-doji-engulf) + grid add
entry_long: candle ID2=doji (body<upper wick and body<lower wick), candle ID1=bullish with body<=100pip, candle ID3=bearish -> buy first order, SL=candle ID2 low, no TP
entry_short: candle ID2=doji, candle ID1=bearish body<=100pip, candle ID3=bullish -> sell first order, SL=candle ID2 high, no TP
exit: first order has SL at doji high/low, no TP; grid-add orders have no SL/TP; whole basket cut-loss at -$10 (close_money)
escalation_cap: cut-loss $10 basket-wide (no per-lot cap)
buildon_idea: already money-capped via $10 basket cut-loss; add explicit max-order count cap and test linear vs log lot law on the grid adds; flat-lot PF test first
novelty_note: 3-candle doji reversal entry signal is a distinctive filter, common grid-add money-management otherwise

title: 7-EMA stacked alignment (forecasting) trend entry
entry_long: EMA1>EMA2>EMA3>EMA4>EMA5>EMA6>EMA7 fully stacked descending-period order, distance(EMA1,EMA7)<=1000pip -> buy, no SL/TP
entry_short: EMA1<EMA2<...<EMA7 fully stacked ascending-period order, distance<=1000pip -> sell, no SL/TP
exit: no SL, no TP, trailing stop 100pip/step5
escalation_cap: n/a

novelty_note: 7-EMA full stack alignment is a fairly rare/strict trend filter vs typical 2-3 EMA crosses

title: RSI overbought/oversold reversal + opposite pending hedge + grid
entry_long: RSI(candle ID1)>=90 and candle ID1 bullish -> buy 0.01 SL100/TP150; simultaneously place pending sell-stop at candle ID1 low; if buy runs, add buy every 100pip (grid)
entry_short: RSI(candle ID1)<=10 and candle ID1 bearish -> sell 0.01 SL100/TP150; simultaneously place pending buy-stop at candle ID1 high; if sell runs, add sell every 100pip (grid)
exit: first order SL100/TP150; grid-add orders no SL/TP, managed by trailing stop 200pip/step5 once >=2 orders on a side
escalation_cap: none stated
buildon_idea: add a max-order or lot cap on the grid-add leg; flat-lot PF check on grid adds; try log-lot law instead of fixed-add
novelty_note: opposite-side pending order placed at same time as the initial contrarian RSI entry (anticipating reversal) is a distinctive idea from a student suggestion

title: Custom-indicator import tutorial (Micro1360 Dynamic MA cross) + grid add
entry_long: custom indicator buffer0 (red) crosses above buffer1 (blue) between candle ID2 and ID1 -> buy 0.01, no SL/TP
entry_short: custom indicator buffer0 crosses below buffer1 between candle ID2 and ID1 -> sell 0.01, no SL/TP
exit: no SL/TP on entries; grid-add every 15pip on adverse move; hard cut via max-order count = 30 orders closes basket
escalation_cap: max 30 orders (basket-wide)

novelty_note: demonstrates importing a 3rd-party custom indicator (not a stock one) as the entry signal; also teaches the FX DMA custom-indicator import workflow

title: ZigZag breakout (structure break) with dynamic buy/sell lines + grid
entry_long: price closes above dynamic drawn 'Line_buy' object (set at ZigZag swing high, 20-candle lookback) -> buy 0.01, SL100, no TP; delete line after entry
entry_short: price closes below dynamic drawn 'Line_sell' object (set at ZigZag swing low) -> sell 0.01, SL100, no TP; delete line after entry
exit: first order SL100 only; grid-add every 50pip on adverse move (no SL/TP on adds); trailing stop 100pip/step10 once >=2 orders on a side
escalation_cap: none stated

novelty_note: uses chart-drawn horizontal line objects (auto-generated at swing points) as the breakout trigger instead of pure indicator-value comparison; simplified redo of a prior example

title: Grid strategy with dynamic average-price TP synchronization (volume-capped)
indicators: price-action grid, no signal indicator (mode B/S toggle only)
entry_long: mode_B=true -> open buy every 100pip grid distance, fixed 0.01 lot, volume_upper_limit set to prevent lot-jump; no SL/TP; TP of whole basket dynamically Modify'd to average_price_B + 50pip
entry_short: mode_S=true -> open sell every 100pip grid distance, fixed 0.01 lot, volume_upper_limit capped; TP dynamically Modify'd to average_price_S - 50pip
exit: basket TP recalculated to breakeven+50pip via average-price formula each add; hard cut-loss at -30% of balance closes both sides
escalation_cap: volume_upper_limit per order + -30% balance basket cut-loss
buildon_idea: already volume-capped and %-balance cut-loss capped; core reusable technique = the average-price/breakeven TP-modify formula, applicable to any grid EA
novelty_note: teaches the general-purpose average-price (breakeven) calculation + auto-repositioning TP technique, explicitly meant to be reused across other EAs

title: Grid trading strategy with dynamic TP-to-average-price sync (trend-mode toggle)
indicators: price-action grid, no signal indicator (mode B/S toggle, recommend trend-following single side)
entry_long: mode_buy=true -> open buy every 100pip grid distance, fixed 0.01 lot, no SL/TP; TP of all buy orders Modify'd to average_price_buy + 50pip
entry_short: mode_sell=true -> open sell every 100pip grid distance, fixed 0.01 lot, no SL/TP; TP Modify'd to average_price_sell - 50pip
exit: basket TP recalculated to breakeven+50pip on each add; hard cut-loss at -30% of balance closes both sides and resets
escalation_cap: -30% balance basket cut-loss (no per-order lot cap)
buildon_idea: author explicitly recommends trend-following single-side use (buy-only in uptrend) for higher efficiency; add per-order lot/volume cap; reusable average-price TP-modify technique for other EAs
novelty_note: same average-price/breakeven TP-modify technique as the companion 126 video, demonstrated with single-side trend-following recommendation and live XAUUSD backtest

title: Dynamic Grid Zone with hedging escape (band +/-1000pip, 3% trigger)
entry_long: mode_B=true and price between dynamic upper/lower band lines (initial band = current price +/-1000pip) -> buy every 100pip grid inside band, 0.01 lot, TP100pip, no SL, volume_upper_limit capped
entry_short: mode_S=true and price inside band -> sell every 100pip grid inside band, 0.01 lot, TP100pip, no SL, volume_upper_limit capped
exit: in-band orders TP100pip each; if price breaks band and floating loss > 3% of balance -> open 1 hedge order sized 2x the trapped opposite-side lots (SL at band line, no TP); basket closes on +$5 profit and band re-centers; alt Cut-Loss-Mode closes basket outright at 3% loss instead of hedging
escalation_cap: volume_upper_limit per grid order + hedge capped at 1 shot (counter-locked) sized 2x trapped lots + 3%-balance trigger
buildon_idea: already has hedge-size logic and a mutually-exclusive cut-loss alternative mode; note author says the 2000pip band is too narrow, widen pip_level; the single-shot 2x hedge is itself capped (counter blocks repeat hedges) but if hedge SL is hit repeatedly the band re-centers without hard total-loss ceiling — verify with flat-lot/no-hedge test first
